title: Orsen and the Sigil Anew
premise: Cyrus Hartwell is a false name; he was born Orsen Vael, the storm-caller who broke the covenant between the mortal realm and the Sigil — the living lattice of magic — twenty years ago, an act for which all magic was outlawed and he was exiled. When the border wards collapse and the stars go out, Orsen must gather the scattered fragments of the broken covenant, each held by someone he wronged or who betrayed him, while the Crown's witch-hunter Maren Solace hunts him and the void beyond the wards devours the sky. The truth of that night — that he shattered the covenant to stop the old kings from feeding it human souls — forces him to choose between clearing his name and saving the realms. In the end, Orsen reforges the covenant not with the kings or the law but with ordinary people, sacrificing his own identity into the Sigil so that magic returns nameless and free, and Maren chooses justice outside the law by letting the world remember him as Cyrus, the charm-seller who saved it.
about_author: Hazel Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing banned grimoires before turning to fiction. She writes from a coastal town where the fog, she insists, is doing something on purpose.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Cyrus Hartwell sells a luck-charm to a frightened child in the city of Greyharrow when every star vanishes at once and the border wards shatter like glass. His hidden storm-magic answers the falling sky unbidden, exposing him. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: dread and the terror of being seen after twenty years of hiding.

chapters.title: Ashes on the Wardline
chapters.summary: Fleeing the city, Cyrus reaches the collapsed wardline and finds the dead wards still whispering his true name: Orsen Vael. Witch-hunter Maren Solace arrives investigating the fall and nearly catches him. POV: Cyrus, with a brief Maren interlude. Emotional beat: hunted, haunted by a name he buried.

chapters.title: What the Charm-Seller Knew
chapters.summary: Maren reconstructs the crime scene and finds traces of storm-calling identical to records of Orsen Vael, the traitor who broke the covenant two decades ago. She begins to suspect the exiled legend never left. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: cold determination curdling into obsession.

chapters.title: The First Fragment
chapters.summary: Cyrus seeks the first covenant fragment held by Sera Ives, his former apprentice who now leads an underground circle of hedge-witches. She agrees to help only if he confesses what really happened that night. He refuses. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: shame weaponized against him by someone he loves.

chapters.title: Hollow Court
chapters.summary: In the capital, the Crown blames the fall on foreign sorcery and declares martial law; Maren is ordered to deliver Orsen's head, not answers. She uncovers a sealed file suggesting the old kings knew the wards would fail. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: loyalty to the law beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The Road Beneath
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Sera travel the smugglers' tunnels toward the second fragment, ambushed by void-touched creatures leaking through the fallen wards. Cyrus uses his storms openly for the first time in twenty years. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: exhilaration and guilt entwined — power feels like coming home.

chapters.title: The King Who Fed the Sky
chapters.summary: A dying elder mage reveals the truth to Sera: the old kings fed prisoners' souls to the covenant to keep it cheap and cruel, and Orsen shattered it to stop them. Sera confronts Cyrus, who finally admits it. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as sacrifice, forgiveness withheld.

chapters.title: Maren's Warrant
chapters.summary: Maren captures Sera and interrogates her, learning enough to doubt the official story of Orsen's treason. Offered promotion for Orsen's head, she requests the sealed royal files instead. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: the first open act of disobedience.

chapters.title: The Second Fragment
chapters.summary: Cyrus retrieves the second fragment from a drowned temple guarded by the ghost of his brother Tam, whom he abandoned during the exile. The ghost demands remembrance, not forgiveness. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: grief as a toll that must be paid honestly.

chapters.title: Stars Going Out Westward
chapters.summary: The void spreads; whole villages go dark and silent. Refugees flood Greyharrow, and the underground circle works openly now, magic returning as the covenant weakens. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: fear transmuting into solidarity among the outlawed.

chapters.title: The Third Fragment
chapters.summary: The third fragment lies in the Crown vault itself. Maren, now officially a traitor, meets Cyrus there by accident — and instead of arresting him, asks him one question: why did you break it? His answer changes her. POV: alternating Maren and Cyrus. Emotional beat: enemies recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Kings Buried
chapters.summary: Maren opens the sealed files: the kings planned to reforge the covenant themselves using mass sacrifice, and needed Orsen found dead before he could speak. Her warrant was always an execution order. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: the law revealed as the true criminal.

chapters.title: Sera's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sera trades herself to the Crown's spymaster to buy Cyrus time, concealing that she carries a forged copy of the third fragment. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: loyalty expressed as sacrifice without martyrdom.

chapters.title: The Gathering Storm
chapters.summary: Cyrus, Maren, and the circle convene at the ruined wardline where the covenant can be reforged — but the final fragment is missing, and the void arrives ahead of schedule. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into acceptance of likely death.

chapters.title: Tam's Voice
chapters.summary: At the wardline, the ghosts of everyone the old kings sacrificed appear, including Tam, who reveals the final fragment was inside Orsen all along — branded into him the night he broke the covenant. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: horror giving way to terrible clarity.

chapters.title: The Spymaster's Trap
chapters.summary: The Crown's forces and the spymaster converge on the wardline with Sera in chains, intending to complete the kings' sacrificial rite themselves. Maren turns her warrant around and arrests the spymaster mid-rite. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: justice seized outside the law.

chapters.title: Orsen Vael
chapters.summary: Before the gathered survivors and ghosts, Cyrus publicly renounces his false name and claims Orsen Vael — owning both his crime and his cause. The void pauses, listening. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed at the worst possible moment.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Orsen begins the reforging, drawing the fragments together while Sera and the circle hold the void back with raw, untrained magic. The rite demands a soul equal to the kings' stolen thousands. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: desperate hope against arithmetic no one can win.

chapters.title: The Nameless Gift
chapters.summary: Orsen offers not his life but his name and history, dissolving 'Orsen Vael' into the covenant so magic belongs to no bloodline and no crown. The stars relight, changed. POV: Cyrus/Orsen, dissolving. Emotional beat: transcendence through self-erasure.

chapters.title: After the Light
chapters.summary: Magic returns quietly to the world — small charms, hedge-healing, rain called gently. Sera leads the new open circles; Maren rebuilds justice from outside the institutions that failed. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: weary, earned peace.

chapters.title: The Charm-Seller's Stall
chapters.summary: In Greyharrow, a stall appears selling small charms, run by a young woman with familiar grey eyes — a fragment of Orsen given human form by the covenant, remembering nothing but kindness. Maren buys a luck-charm and says nothing. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: bittersweet grace.

chapters.title: Sigil Anew
chapters.summary: Sera writes the true history into the new covenant's memory so no king can twist it again, and the book closes on the child from chapter one calling a small, harmless storm just to watch it sparkle. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: wonder restored, vigilance promised.
